chapter: Chords, recordings and his own groups
title: Learning to read and writing the block-chord book
summary: He taught himself to read from a small book, and his book puts a chord under every note, for piano, six-string and vibes.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: So were you reading chords then?

... No, the first time I ever thought about it must have been about '68 or '69. ... I say, "damn, everybody always ask me can I read this, can I read that. So I got no teacher, so I got a little old book. So I set myself up there with that book and count and one and two and three. See, the funny part it is one is all right but "and" is a pretty mean broad. ... But I get that, and I got a few more cues, and then I had to learn my fingerboard pretty good. ... As far as the reading thing, I finally got so I could read fairly good. I read good enough to write this book. And I can take a song like Caravan, that doesn't have any song chords. See, my belief is puttin' a chord to every note & that's very seldom -- Even Johnny Smith couldn't do that. ... My thing is to have no single notes nowhere as far as the first chorus is concerned. Every note is a chord. Sometimes its down to two or three notes, but its still a chord. ... So that's what my book is about, and its for piano and six string and luckily, 4 string, but mostly for vibraphone players. Vibes couldn't handle it, and be playin' the same thing, those ballads with 3 and 4 mallets at a time. ... That's what I'm working on as far as the book is concerned.
